title: Paper Substrate Curl Recovery
researchQuestion: How does a short indoor conditioning interval affect the visible curl recovery of common uncoated office paper?
summary: This study uses ordinary office paper and a flat indoor surface to see whether visible curl recovery can be recorded consistently outside a laboratory. The current observation period is underway and is not accepting additional participants.
eligibility: Access to ordinary, untreated office paper and a clean, dry, flat indoor surface.
Able to leave the sample undisturbed for forty-eight hours.
A household relative-humidity display may be used but is not required.
exclusions: Coated, thermal, archival, chemically treated, wet, contaminated, or personally significant paper is excluded.
No heat source, chemical, liquid application, or enclosed high-humidity treatment is permitted.
participantActivities: Prepare one ordinary sheet using the specified dry fold-and-release sequence and place it on a clean flat surface.
At four assigned intervals, select the closest categorical edge-height reference without touching or weighting the sheet.
Record whether the sample was disturbed and, when available, the room's displayed relative-humidity category.

protocolSteps.title: Prepare
protocolSteps.description: Use one clean untreated sheet and the specified dry fold-and-release sequence.

protocolSteps.title: Condition
protocolSteps.description: Place the sample on a dry flat surface and leave it unweighted and undisturbed.

protocolSteps.title: Observe
protocolSteps.description: Select the nearest categorical edge-height reference at four assigned intervals.

protocolSteps.title: Review
protocolSteps.description: Mark any disturbance and check the observation sequence for missed intervals.

dataRequested: Broad paper weight and surface category.
Categorical edge-height observation at each assigned interval.
Broad indoor relative-humidity category when a display is available.
Confirmation that the sample remained undisturbed.
dataNotRequested: Paper brand, purchase information, printed content, photographs, or physical samples.
Home or workplace address, room identity, or information about occupants.
Use of chemicals, liquids, heat, or powered test equipment.
samplePrompts: Which edge-height reference most closely matches the highest free corner?
Was the sheet moved, touched, or weighted since the preceding observation?
Is a room relative-humidity category available at this interval?
methodNotes: Categorical edge references are used instead of improvised precision measurement so the method remains consistent with ordinary household materials.
The protocol uses only dry mechanical preparation and ambient indoor conditioning.
Samples that are disturbed or exposed to liquid are closed without replacement observations.
limitations: Paper manufacture, prior storage, room conditions, and flatness of the reference surface vary between observations.
Categorical edge height is a screening measure and is not a substitute for laboratory dimensional-stability testing.
The protocol can describe recovery patterns but cannot assign a manufacturing cause.
